item.title: Playing with Fire. A Tale of Saboteurs
item.description: They committed crimes against their own country in exchange for rewards from Ukrainian intelligence, but the promised money never came. Instead, each of them ended up with a prison sentence including years behind bars.They were all given assignments by Ukrainian intelligence agents. Aleksey from Orenburg planned to do harm to railway tracks. Eduard from Krasnodar was preparing to blow up a petrol station. item.title: Intervision: Happy Moments
item.description: Last year, Moscow hosted the Intervision music contest, with 23 nations taking part. The participants faced a demanding task: in their 3 minutes on stage, they had to do more than just sing – they had to convey the traditions and cultural spirit of their home countries.The performers themselves said they had not come to Russia in search of trophies. item.title: Kostroma Ballet. A Family Affair
item.description: The Kostroma Russian National Ballet is more than just a dance company – it is a close-knit creative family. Founded in 1991 by Elena and Yury Tsarenko, it has become one of the country’s best-known cultural ensembles, earning international recognition.The troupe’s choreography and staging upend stereotypes, combining classical ballet with the richness of Russian folk dance. item.title: Heroes of Fire
item.description: Emergency service crews are the first to confront the aftermath of shelling by Ukrainian drones and artillery. Every call-out could be their last, as they are deliberately targeted by the enemy. In this documentary, filmmakers capture the demanding work of rescuers in Gorlovka and Donetsk.Every firefighter has a personal story. item.title: Soul Renovation: Donbass Churches Rebuilt
item.description: A story about the indomitable spirit of Orthodoxy and the power of human faith. Churches throughout Donbass are currently being restored alongside homes destroyed by war. For many believers, seeing these sacred sites rebuilt helps heal souls wounded by conflict.

item.title: Bloody Puppets of the West
item.description: A new type of female politician is rising to power in the West. The common trait these ambitious women all share is an insatiable thirst for power. They include Ursula von der Leyen, Annalena Baerbock, Liz Truss, and Miroslava Němcová, the last of whom even called for repeating the Siege of Leningrad on social media. Who is nurturing these ruthless figures and to what end? Find the answers in this film by Tatiana Borshch.

item.title: Hands That Restore the World
item.description: They are changing the world around them. People working to bring the cultural heritage of their ancestors back to life lie at the heart of this film.Farid Nabiullin spent years travelling to remote villages in Tatarstan in search of horses with distinctive white manes – the last of a rare breed known as ‘celestial golden horses’. item.title: Donbass: Truth in the Crosshairs
item.description: Their reports are banned back home. Criminal cases have been opened against them, and their social media and bank accounts have been blocked. Yet they refuse to be silenced and continue to tell the world the truth about the conflict in Ukraine. item.title: The Big Picture: Migrant Mayors
item.description: New York has elected a mayor who was born abroad for the very first time. Zohran Mamdani is a practising Muslim who became a US citizen just eight years ago. His opponents accuse him of antisemitism, while Donald Trump went so far as to brand him a ‘communist lunatic’.
